correctness.rationale: A 2-dimensional subspace of a six-dimensional vector space over the binary field has exactly three nonzero vectors. Selecting the two smallest bit masks gives one canonical basis of each of the 651 planes. Any rank-two linear map is thereby represented uniquely by one of the 3906 ordered independent functional pairs on one plane; there are 2,542,806 total candidates. The Rota–Baxter identity is bilinear, so evaluation on all 36 basis pairs is necessary and sufficient. Two compiled standalone exhaustive checkers implement distinct canonical map representations and independently construct matrix multiplication, both reproducing all six fiber frequencies, 58 active planes and 652 passing operators. The two largest fibers, 210 each, also follow from a direct square-zero-ideal/surjection argument. No infinite extrapolation is asserted.

value.rationale: The first binary rank-two layer after the known rank-one classification is a complete natural rank stratum of the weight-zero Rota–Baxter variety on the six-dimensional triangular algebra. The enumeration is not an arbitrary selected subset: every one of 2,542,806 rank-two maps and every one of the 651 possible image planes is checked. The nontrivial six-level fiber profile and the concentration of 420 of 652 operators on exactly two intrinsic square-zero ideals offer a structural phenomenon and a reference point for future field/rank enumeration. Exact finite cutoffs are mathematically motivated by the characteristic-zero classification boundary.
